title: Detecting open orbits of faithful connected solvable actions with nontrivial unipotents by bounded generalized root subgroups in characteristic zero
source_title: Characterizing smooth affine spherical varieties via the automorphism group
author: Andriy Regeta; Immanuel van Santen
difficulty_reason: The cited rational quotient and solvable invariant-fraction results do not by themselves produce root subgroups of a prescribed common weight and arbitrarily large dimension. The author combines two equal-weight semi-invariants with a homogeneous additive action to construct the displayed replicated actions, and verifies faithfulness through the independence of their homogeneous powers. That same-weight replication construction supplies the unbounded family needed for the converse implication, together with the exact vector-field/root-subgroup comparison.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Independent Proposition7.3 over algebraically closed characteristic0 field: irreducible quasi-affine X, faithful action of connected solvable B containing nontrivial unipotent elements. Exact equivalence with bounded semi-invariant vector-field spaces and bounded generalized root subgroups retained. Complete author construction of arbitrarily large faithful same-weight additive subgroups from two equal-weight semi-invariants supplied. Rosenlicht rational quotient and the stated solvable invariant-fraction theorem are explicit standard prerequisites. Replication preserves the action because the semi-invariants are invariant under its unipotent subgroup (characters of a connected unipotent group are trivial); this is a bounded standard detail of the explicit displayed action. No reductive reconstruction theorem, arbitrary torus-action criterion, or classification by abstract automorphism groups asserted.
